tags.gist: Says the two axes can work like probability times consequence if detectability and humans in the loop are added, calling traceability impossible for opaque models.
Repeats that the framework can function with a detectability layer and human oversight included, and that traceability is unachievable given model opacity.
Treats directive outputs as medical advice and wants all non-FDA-approved outputs marked for information only with required linguistic modifiers.
Calls patient-facing use unequivocally higher risk and rejects patient empowerment as a goal, since idiosyncratic self-application cannot be regulated.
Wants outputs to carry modifiers telling generalists the content is designed for specialists, lest they act on it under a general license.
Wants the model to recognize when it drifts into advice, withhold it from the patient, and warn that the exchange has moved into that territory.
Argues over-escalation, an error of commission, can be more dangerous than under-escalation, an error of omission.
Finds the competency approach useful and appropriate, covering the bulk of submissions despite edge cases.
Says available external guidelines are insufficient to leverage, while the non-agentic benchmarking elements are robust enough.
Calls the single agentic benchmarking element inadequate because it does not probe what the agent does or how deeply enough.
Wants FDA to give sponsors a starting data framework rather than bespoke builds, to steer them away from contamination, saturation and overfitting.
Wants confirmation chosen through a risk framework that weighs therapeutic area, patient exposure and real-world use cases.
Would treat synthetic distributions as the control and require real-world distributions to differ meaningfully in clinical and practical significance.
Thinks synthetic subpopulations could suit any non-rare condition, provided they derive from literature meta-analyses rather than single studies.
Wants meta-analytic data as comparators, with a mix of generalists and specialists as the standard, analyzed like a gauge repeatability study.
Considers no intervention the only reliable absence-of-device comparator, the others being too unpredictable.
Calls a third-party requirement inadvisable because it invites gaming and profit centers that draw out testing.
Wants each architecture assessed, with multimodal vision-language models categorized as higher risk under the agentic element.
